summary: Partial stream outputs and missing terminal punctuation after mid-stream stall behind enterprise SOCKS proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running SSE sessions from their mobile app frequently end with partial outputs (missing final punctuation or truncated last sentence) following a short network stall. After the stall, the client sometimes reconnects and receives duplicate prefixes but is still missing the terminal punctuation or closing sentence. This is blocking Parcelly's delivery-notification feature for ~5% of heavy users.

Impact:
- Intermittent user-visible truncation of generated messages (missing final sentence or period).
- Visible on the customer's dedicated deployment in us-east; affects mobile app behind enterprise SOCKS proxy.
- Occurs for long streaming responses (>12s), higher incidence on cellular+VPN.

Environment:
- Customer dedicated cluster (dedicated pool), region: us-east-1, prod.
- Client: Parcelly Android app v3.4.1, corporate SOCKS5 proxy + VPN.
- Server-side model: redwood-open-7b-v1, streaming SSE endpoint /v1/stream.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1. Start a long-form generation prompt that yields >250 tokens (~15s).
2. Put device onto cellular with enterprise SOCKS+VPN active.
3. Trigger a brief backgrounding or network flap (toggle airplane mode for 2-4s).
4. App reconnects and resumes the SSE session.

Observed behavior:
- Stream resumes but the final sentence is either truncated or the terminal punctuation is missing.
- Occasionally the client sees a duplicated prefix chunk (last 10-30 tokens) and then no concluding token.
- No explicit 5xx from API; connection shows FIN/ACK from intermediate proxy in some packet captures.

Expected behavior:
- Client should receive a complete finalization event (server-sent end marker or explicit choice 'finalized' frame) and full text for the choice, or the resumed session should produce the remaining tokens to close the choice.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- Packet capture (pcap) showing mid-stream FIN from proxy: trace_id=tr-20260310-8f2a
- Client SDK logs with session id: sess-7a9f-22, timestamps and last-received-token-index=243.
- Example truncated output and original expected complete output.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:02 - Aisha Kumar: Initial triage - customer provided pcap and SDK logs. No 5xx from Redwood. Packet capture shows FIN from enterprise proxy shortly after stall (see tr-20260310-8f2a). Escalating to networking and serving runtime teams.

2026-03-10 13:45 - Diego Morales: Reproduced locally using the customer's repro steps behind a SOCKS5 proxy + small MTU. Observed identical behavior: server continued to send tail tokens but proxy sent FIN causing the client to re-establish and miss the terminal event. Created ephemeral trace id tr-internal-0310-2.

2026-03-11 09:10 - SRE (Marta Higgins): Hypothesis: proxy or VPN teardown triggers a half-close where small buffered tail fragments are dropped. Client reconnect logic then replays prefix but server-side finalization event was lost and isn't retried due to idempotency semantics. Suggest adding explicit server-side finalize frame that can be requested by client on reconnect.

2026-03-11 15:22 - Solutions Eng (Ravi Patel): Customer attempted client workaround: send periodic application-level keepalive (1s) to prevent proxy from closing mid-stream; reduced incidence to ~0.5% in their beta. They prefer an SDK/server-side change for robust handling.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Diego Morales: Created a small server-side patch proposal to emit a finalization control event with sequence numbers and idempotency token. PR referenced in related_github_prs. Pending review by runtime team.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Customer (Parcelly): Accepts keepalive workaround short-term and requests ETA for permanent fix. Asking to retain session replay metadata in dedicated pool for 48h.
investigation_notes:
Findings so far: (1) No 5xx or application error logged in the Redwood runtime for trace tr-20260310-8f2a; logs show tokens streamed up to token index 246, then client-driven reconnect. (2) Packet captures demonstrate an intermediate proxy FIN/ACK sequence very close to the final tokens being emitted. (3) The server currently treats streaming as best-effort: if the connection drops before finalization event is ACKed, the model-generating worker does not automatically emit the remaining tokens to the resumed session because resume uses an idempotency token that assumes last ACK. (4) Client-side keepalive reduced occurrences in customer test. (5) Reproduced locally by inducing socket half-close and rapid reconnection via SOCKS.
Hypothesis: Enterprise proxy performs aggressive half-close or reassembly and drops last N small TCP segments containing finalization boundary; our resume protocol doesn't include a way for the client to request 'give me remainder since token #N' if server didn't persist remainder.
resolution:
Workarounds: (1) Customer to enable application-level keepalives at 1s or enable SDK option 'stream_keepalive' to reduce proxy idle close behavior. (2) Recommend customer increase proxy idle timeout where possible.
Planned permanent fix: implement server-side finalization events combined with sequence numbers and idempotency bounds so resumed sessions can request missing token ranges. Patch PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-client-fixes/pull/142. Target: canary deploy to dedicated clusters in us-east by 2026-03-20.
Follow-ups: add monitoring for rate of truncated finalization events per cluster and expose metric in Console. Retain session metadata for 48h behind dedicated pool per customer request.
next_steps: 1) Communicate short-term workaround to Parcelly (Aisha): enable SDK keepalive and increase proxy timeout if possible. 2) Runtime team to review PR and schedule canary for dedicated clusters. 3) SRE to add alert for 'stream-finalization-missing' metric. 4) Track customer impact until permanent fix is deployed.
customer_impact_summary: Parcelly's delivery-notification messages sometimes end mid-sentence for a small but meaningful subset of mobile users on enterprise VPNs. Workaround reduces occurrence; permanent server-side fix is being scheduled.
notes_for_postmortem: If PR is insufficient, expand to: (a) persist finalization buffer server-side for short window (48h) to allow client re-request, (b) ensure finalization frames are sent over multiple transport windows or marked for high-priority delivery. Include test harness that simulates proxy half-close and validates reassembly of finalization frame.
